questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people, being alone in a new city and exploring a different culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Because the semester doesn't officially start until October, I would recommend taking a language course in september to meet people before uni starts.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The uni provides you with a lot of information through emails, there are intro days and if you have further questions they assign you a coordinator that you can always email. I

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There is an eramsus office that can help you if you don't have a place to stay etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky and had a friend, whos room i could rent. I would check facebook groups for Danes in Berlin for available rooms.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Campus is a bit outside of the city, and it can take a while to get there, so bear that in mind when you find your acomodation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very happy with my place, and most of my friends found good places too.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They change their courses every semester, so it took a while to get my OLA confirmed. I would recomend just picking some classes you know will be approved so you can get your eramsus grant, and then change it as soon as you know what classes you are actually gonna take.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: If you take courses in your own institution its pretty easy, you can do it online, but if you wanna take courses outside your institution you need to email the professor and in the end of the semester they will sign a pdf that verifies you took the course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You have 2 weeks to test out different courses, so if you don't like the courses you picked it's easy to drop them and pick something different.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start off with more classes than you need, and then drop the ones you don't find interesting. Also you get different amounts of ECTS points according to what kind of exam you do. I would recommend a few long exams instead of many short ones.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was many interesting courses to choose from. I only wanted courses in english, so the options were more limited, but the JFKI institute came through.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was more or less the same level as KU, depending on the course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Depended a lot on the course, but more work during the semester than at KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Jane Austen's Novels, Investigating Representations of Race, Gender, and Queer Identity in News, Communication Skills: Speaking Your Mind: Public Speaking and Presentation Skills and Digital Games in Contemporary American Culture.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Michael Auer and Ruth Wishart are great professors, i would check their courses out.

questions.answer: Food is really cheap, especially if you don't eat meat.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a big selection of sports through Unisports and its pretty cheap.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: lots of sports, idk about social clubs I didn't hear about them. JFKI has a bar every Wednesday kind of like fredagsbar.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Unisports or radio such as cashmere (not through uni tho)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It's easy  and free to move around by train, so visit nearby cities like potsdam.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy, very similar to Denmark

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: talk to people in your courses and tru not to have classes back to back, so you can eat lunch together etc.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: be open, don't be scared of all the bureaucracy and try the japanese mensa at uni.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I had a lot of trouble with my landlord, but keep in mind that german laws almost always take the tenant's side. You can get help from a Mieterverein and it's cheap to become a member.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: New friendships and experiences

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Meeting people before the semester started

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
